findings.evidence: Basic.lean:36 `∫ x in Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, x ^ n * f i x Q2`; Basic.lean:163 proof is `simp only [mellinMoment, h]`, which only rewrites under the set integral. Mathlib states the general form on the integration domain: `mathlib/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Integral/Bochner/Set.lean:73 theorem setIntegral_congr_fun (hs : MeasurableSet s) (h : EqOn f g s)`.
findings.fix: Weaken to `(h : Set.EqOn (fun x => f i x Q2) (fun x => g j x Q2) (Set.Icc 0 1))` and prove by `MeasureTheory.setIntegral_congr_fun measurableSet_Icc fun x hx => by rw [h hx]`.
findings.issue: `mellinMoment_congr` assumes `∀ x, f i x Q2 = g j x Q2`, but `mellinMoment` (line 36) is `∫ x in Set.Icc (0:ℝ) 1, x ^ n * f i x Q2`, so only equality on `Icc 0 1` is used. The hypothesis is strictly stronger than the proof needs and than the Mathlib convention for integral congruence.

findings.evidence: ChargeConjugation.lean:159-160: hypothesis `∀ x, ...`, proof `rw [valenceNumber_def, mellinMoment_congr h, sub_self]` — the only use is through `mellinMoment_congr`. `IsPartonDensity` (Basic.lean:95-99) constrains a density only on `[0,1]`, so off-support values are arbitrary data a caller should not have to control.
findings.fix: State the hypothesis as `Set.EqOn (f (.quark i) · Q2) (f (.antiquark i) · Q2) (Set.Icc 0 1)` once `mellinMoment_congr` is weakened; `valenceNumber_eq_zero_of_chargeConj_eq` then supplies the `EqOn` from `congr_fun₃ h` restricted to the interval and is unaffected.
findings.issue: `valenceNumber_eq_zero_of_quark_eq_antiquark` inherits the same too-strong hypothesis: it requires `f (.quark i) x Q2 = f (.antiquark i) x Q2` for every real `x`, including outside the physical support, while `valenceNumber` only sees `Icc 0 1`. A caller holding a density relation on the unit interval — the form roadmap §1.3 states its pion relations in, "at every momentum fraction" — cannot apply it without first manufacturing the off-support equality from `IsPartonDensity.support`.

summary: The pullback API is now at the right level and every charge-conjugation result is derived from it, resolving the earlier findings. What remains is that `mellinMoment_congr` demands density equality at every real `x` although the moment integrates only over `Set.Icc 0 1`, and `valenceNumber_eq_zero_of_quark_eq_antiquark` inherits that too-strong hypothesis.
